messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: fill in layer_bar() - reprise
parts:
Hi Winston and Hadley,

This time I *am* using the latest version, as of this morning.

The issue is that fill does not seem to correspond with the underlying data.

Code below. Happy to file a github issue if you like.

Thanks,

Ian


dragon <- read.csv(
  header = TRUE,  
  text = "rider_gender,dragon_size,time
          male,big,6.7
          male,big,7.5
          male,small,4.5
          female,small,6.5
          female,small,6.3
          female,big,6.8"
)

# check out the numbers here
dragon %>% group_by(rider_gender, dragon_size) %>% summarize(count = n())

# dragon_size seems to be reversed
dragon %>% ggvis(x = ~rider_gender, fill = ~dragon_size) %>% layer_bars()

dragon_mod <- 
  dragon %>%
  mutate(
    rider_gender = factor(rider_gender), 
    dragon_size = factor(dragon_size)
  )

# dragon_size still reversed
dragon_mod %>% ggvis(x = ~rider_gender, fill = ~dragon_size) %>% layer_bars()

messages.subject: Re: fill in layer_bar() - reprise
parts:
Hi Winston,

Legend order different from stacking order isn't what I had in mind, but happy to file an issue there.

The issue is that the plot indicates that two females are associated with big dragons, one with small; but the numbers indicate two females are associated with *small* dragons and one with big.

Dataset adapted from [The Cartoon Introduction to Statistics](http://amzn.com/0809033593) by Grady Klein and Alan Dabney, in case you were wondering :)

Attached png.
